What we confirmed on official pages

  • Taxes due Jan 1; first half accepted without penalty until April 30, second half until October 31; delinquent May 1 and Nov 1
  • Late payments: 10% annual penalty (.83333 per month); must be postmarked by Apr 30/Oct 31; online payments count as paid on transaction date

What we could not confirm

Minnehaha County by the numbers

Minnehaha County ranks 1 of 3 South Dakota counties in this guide by population, at about 200,689 people in 87,043 housing units (Census Bureau, 2019-2023). At $266,600, the median home value sits 19% above the South Dakota county median for this guide. The South Dakota county median income is $70,101, and Minnehaha County reports $76,074. Owner-occupancy is 64%, so renters hold about 36% of occupied homes.

What is Minnehaha County, South Dakota, like?

Minnehaha County is South Dakota's most populous county, on the state's eastern border, and Sioux Falls is both its county seat and the state's largest city. It touches Minnesota on the east and the northern and western edge of Iowa, and the Big Sioux River flows south-southeast through its east-central part.

The county was created on April 5, 1862 and organized in 1868. It covers about 814 square miles of mostly rolling farmland with lakes and ponds in the west, and the name comes from a Sioux word meaning rapid water or waterfall. The population grew from 355 in 1870 to 197,214 in the 2020 census. Incorporated places besides Sioux Falls are Baltic, Brandon, Colton, Crooks, Dell Rapids, Garretson, Hartford and Valley Springs.

FactMinnehaha County
County seatSioux Falls
CreatedApril 5, 1862
Total area813.861 square miles
Population, 2020 census197,214
Population, 2019-2023 surveyabout 200,689
Housing units, 2019-202387,043
Median home value, 2019-2023$266,600
Owner-occupied homes64%

What drives the Minnehaha County economy?

Health care leads. The Sioux Falls Development Foundation's major employers list, updated in June 2026, puts Sanford Health with the Evangelical Lutheran Good Samaritan Society at 11,000 to 11,500 employees and Avera Health at 9,500 to 10,000, ahead of every other employer in the city.

Behind them come the Sioux Falls School District at 3,500 to 4,000, Smithfield Foods at 3,000 to 3,500, and Amazon and Hy-Vee at 2,000 to 2,500 each. Banks and financial firms such as Citi, Wells Fargo and First PREMIER Bank each report 1,000 to 1,500. Augustana University, Daktronics and Minnehaha County itself are on the list too.

For a seller, this mix means a rental or inherited house competes in a metro market with large hospital, school and bank workforces nearby. A cash offer can matter most when a house needs work that a retail buyer would not finance.

Which Minnehaha County offices do I deal with?

The Equalization office values your property, the Treasurer collects the tax and the Register of Deeds records the sale. The county's own FAQ explains the split: the Director of Equalization appraises and assesses under state law, the Treasurer bills and collects, and the Auditor calculates tax from the budgets that elected officials set.

  • Treasurer: 415 N. Dakota Ave., Sioux Falls, SD 57104, open 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on weekdays except legal holidays. Phone (605) 367-4211.
  • Director of Equalization: phone (605) 367-4228. It handles assessed values and owner-occupied status. The Treasurer has no say over assessments.
  • Register of Deeds: 415 N. Dakota Ave., first floor, open 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

The Treasurer's office says it is busiest on Mondays and Fridays, on the first business day of the month and the last two, and the day after a holiday. Plan a closing-week payment for a quieter day. You can start on the county Treasurer FAQ page.

When are Minnehaha County property taxes due?

Property taxes are due January 1, and the county accepts the first half without penalty through April 30 and the second half through October 31. They become delinquent on May 1 and November 1, and a late payment carries a 10% annual penalty of .83333% per month.

A payment is late if it is not postmarked by April 30 or October 31, and online payments count as paid on the transaction date. If either date lands on a weekend or holiday, pay by 4:45 p.m. on the last working day. The drop box and online payments work until midnight. The office does not accept early payments and gives no early-payment discount.

  • Mail: 415 N. Dakota Ave., Sioux Falls, SD 57104, with the statement stub or the address, parcel number or bill number. Without that, the payment is returned.
  • Drop box: open around the clock outside the west doors of the County Administration Building.
  • Online: card payments carry a 2.35% convenience fee, shown as a separate charge, and online payments can take 7 to 10 business days to post.
  • Delinquent taxes cannot be paid online. Call (605) 367-4211.
  • Checks must have a pre-printed, in-state name and address.

The delinquency dates match state law. SDCL 10-21-23 says half of the unpaid tax is delinquent on May 1, and the remainder on November 1 if it is not paid by October 31.

How does Minnehaha County value a home?

The legal assessment date is November 1 of every year, and the condition of the property that day sets the assessment for the following year. A house that is half built on November 1 is assessed at half. Residential land is commonly valued by front footage, acreages by the acre, and buildings by quality, size, design and condition, with a finished basement adding value.

Appraisers receive a copy of every building permit issued by a city or the county planning office and review those properties. General maintenance such as a new roof or siding typically does not change the assessment. The county's rough estimate for a new project is the cost, including labor, multiplied by the current tax rate.

State rules then convert value to tax. Taxable value is set at 85% of full and true value, and each taxing unit divides its unfunded budget by the taxable value in its area to find its levy. Owner-occupied homes are a separate classification. The home must be owned and occupied on November 1, and a new owner has to apply between November 1 and March 15.

How do I appeal a Minnehaha County assessment?

Contact the Director of Equalization first. The office can have an appraiser review the property, and the page points to a county Appeal Process Guide for the formal route. A written appeal then goes to the local board, which for Sioux Falls residents is the city's Local Board of Equalization, or to the county board.

StepDate in the 2025 state guide
Written appeal to local board clerkMarch 13 (postmark counts)
Local board meetsMarch 17 to 21
Appeal to county auditorApril 1
County board of equalization sitsApril 8 to 29
Letter to Office of Hearing ExaminersMay 16
Circuit court appealWithin 30 days of notice

For 2026 the Sioux Falls clerk set March 12 as the deadline for a written notice and scheduled the local board for the week of March 16 to 20. Minnehaha County hearings are held in the Commission Chambers on the third floor at 415 N. Dakota Ave. An owner cannot take the same dispute to the hearing examiners and circuit court at once.

What does it cost to record a sale in Minnehaha County?

Recording a deed costs $30, and the state real estate transfer fee is $1.00 per thousand, or $0.50 per $500 of value. The Register of Deeds lists these on its fee page, and SDCL 43-4-21 sets the transfer fee, which applies to deeds only when there is consideration.

  • Documents over 50 pages add $2.00 per extra page.
  • Copies are $1.00 per page and certification is $5.00.
  • A plat is $60 and a master deed is $75.
  • A federal tax lien or its release is $20, while a state tax lien is recorded at no charge.

On a $266,600 sale, which equals the county's median home value, the transfer fee would be about $267. The Register of Deeds does not give legal advice, so a title company or attorney should prepare the deed.

If taxes are due at the same time, the Treasurer's payoff figure drives the closing statement. We buy Minnehaha County houses as-is and can work from that number, including houses with repair needs or tenants.

More questions about Minnehaha County, SD Property Tax Guide

When are property taxes due in Minnehaha County?

Taxes are due January 1. The first half is accepted without penalty through April 30 and the second half through October 31, and unpaid halves turn delinquent on May 1 and November 1.

What is the penalty for paying Minnehaha County taxes late?

A 10% annual penalty, or .83333% per month, applies. A mailed payment counts as on time only if it is postmarked by April 30 or October 31.

Who sets my Minnehaha County property value?

The Director of Equalization sets it, not the Treasurer. Call (605) 367-4228 about values, owner-occupied status and appeals. The legal assessment date is November 1.

How much is the South Dakota transfer fee on a home sale?

It is $0.50 per $500 of value, or $1.00 per $1,000, collected when the deed is recorded. Recording the deed itself costs $30 in Minnehaha County.

Can I sell a Minnehaha County house with unpaid property tax?

Yes. The Treasurer can give you a payoff figure, and the balance is paid from the sale proceeds at closing. Delinquent taxes cannot be paid online, so call the office.

  • Taxes due Jan 1, paid one year in arrears; 1st half delinquent after April 30, 2nd half after October 31 (if weekend, last working day); interest per SDCL 54-3-16
  • Delinquent: tax certificate issued; tax sale third Monday of December if authorized (none in 2023); $40 returned-payment fee; interest/penalty per SDCL 10-21-23 and 10-21-25

Pennington County by the numbers

Pennington County ranks 2 of 3 South Dakota counties in this guide by population, at about 112,081 people in 50,655 housing units (Census Bureau, 2019-2023). At $270,400, the median home value sits 20% above the South Dakota county median for this guide. The South Dakota county median income is $70,101, and Pennington County reports $70,768. Owner-occupancy is 69%, so renters hold about 31% of occupied homes. The median home was built in 1982, about 41 years ago.

Where is Pennington County, South Dakota?

Pennington County is in western South Dakota on the Wyoming line, with Rapid City as the county seat and largest city. Its western end holds Black Elk Peak at 7,242 feet, the highest point east of the Continental Divide, while the northeast corner drops to 1,896 feet, and the Cheyenne River and Rapid Creek drain the county.

At 2,784 square miles it is the state's third-largest county by area and larger than Delaware. It was created on January 11, 1875 and organized on April 19, 1877, and it is named for John L. Pennington, the fifth Governor of Dakota Territory. The county seat began at the mining camp of Sheridan and moved to Rapid City in 1878. Other incorporated places are Box Elder, Hill City and New Underwood. The 2020 census counted 109,222 people, and the Census estimate for 2025 is 116,792.

Settlement followed gold. George Custer's 1874 expedition entered the Black Hills and reported gold, which set off a rush that violated the 1868 Second Treaty of Fort Laramie with the Sioux Nation. Work on Mount Rushmore began in 1927, and the county's later growth rests on tourism and the air base.

What does the Pennington County economy rest on?

Tourism, Ellsworth Air Force Base and health care carry the local economy. A 2025 Minneapolis Fed article on the Rapid City area says tourism is the economic lifeblood, with visitor spending of $1.2 billion in 2023, about 12% of area output, and that Ellsworth, with about 4,100 personnel, is the area's largest employer.

The base began as an Army training airbase shortly after the United States entered World War II. The same article projects personnel rising to 6,300 and settling at 5,900 as B-21 bombers arrive, and reports $1.2 billion in committed construction. Health care is about 14% of area output, and the main provider, Monument Health, serves roughly 450,000 people. Unemployment has averaged 2% or less since 2022, and the 65-and-older group is about a fifth of the population.

Those facts shape selling. A base with a changing workforce and a large older population can mean houses that must sell on a fixed timeline, such as a military move or an estate.

Which Pennington County offices handle my tax?

The Treasurer and the Equalization Department both work from 900 Concourse Drive in Rapid City, and the county footer lists weekday hours of 7:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. The Treasurer's number is 605-394-2163 and Equalization is 605-394-2175.

  • In person: 900 Concourse Drive, Suite 150, Rapid City. Cash, check, money order, debit and credit are accepted.
  • Mail: PO Box 6160, Rapid City, SD 57709-6160, postmarked by the due date.
  • Drop boxes: 130 Kansas City Street and 900 Concourse Drive, listed as available in April and October.
  • Online: current-year taxes only, through Paymentus, with no payments over $25,000 and 3 to 4 days to post.

Fees apply. An online e-check costs $1.95, a card costs 2%, and a returned payment costs $40. The county says neither the Treasurer nor the Board of Commissioners can waive interest and late fees.

When are Pennington County taxes due and what happens if they go unpaid?

Pennington County taxes are paid one year in arrears, so payments made in 2024 cover 2023 taxes, and notices usually go out in late December or early January. The first half is delinquent after April 30 and the second after October 31, and if a deadline falls on a weekend the last working day of the month applies.

Interest starts on the first business day after the deadline at the rate in SDCL 54-3-16. Unpaid taxes after October 31 lead to a tax certificate on the property. The Treasurer can assign certificates or hold an annual tax sale only if the commissioners authorize it. When held, the sale takes place on the third Monday of December, and none was held in 2023. Tax deed proceedings may begin three years after the certificate sale and at any time up to six years after it, under SDCL 10-25.

  • Partial payments and payment plans for delinquent taxes are not accepted.
  • Delinquent taxes require certified funds, and the Treasurer must give the payoff amount.
  • Special assessments are due in full before May 1 and are not split into halves.
  • If a mortgage company pays your taxes, the notice you receive is for information only, and you should confirm the county received the payment.

What relief programs does Pennington County offer?

Two programs matter to older owners: the elderly and disabled assessment freeze and the homestead deferral, and both applications are due April 1 each year. The freeze holds the assessed value of a qualifying homeowner's property at the value from the applicant's qualifying year under SDCL 10-6A, covering the house, garage and lot, or one acre, whichever is less.

The homestead program defers property tax payments until the property is sold, with interest at a reduced rate. A seller who used it should ask the Treasurer for a payoff, because the deferred tax comes due when the house is sold.

Owner-occupied status is separate. The property must be your primary residence, you may claim only one in the state, and you file with the Director of Equalization by March 15.

How do I appeal a Pennington County assessment?

An appeal argues that the assessed value is too high, unequal to similar homes or based on wrong property data, and it is not a complaint about the tax amount. The county's own page gives the 2026 dates and says they apply to 2026 only.

Step2026 date
City property: written notice to local board clerk or EqualizationMarch 12
Local board of equalization meetsMarch 16 to 20
Local board decisions mailedMarch 27
Appeal to county board, or county property noticeApril 7
County board meetsApril 14 to May 5
County board decisions mailedMay 8
Hearing Examiners, or circuit court within 30 daysMay 15

The county's steps are to review your notice, talk to the Equalization Department about comparable sales, file the written appeal, schedule an inspection and then accept or reject the appraiser's recommendation. The office at 900 Concourse Drive is open weekdays from 7:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

What should a Pennington County seller know about closing?

Get a payoff figure from the Treasurer, then have a title company record the deed. The state transfer fee is $0.50 per $500 of value under SDCL 43-4-21, and it applies to deeds only when there is consideration. Recording fees, such as $30 per document under SDCL 7-9-15, are set by statute, but confirm the Pennington County amounts with its Register of Deeds.

The median home in the county was built in 1982, so many houses are decades old, and an older roof or heating system is the kind of item a buyer's inspector flags. We buy Pennington County houses as-is and with no repairs, which helps when the work would cost more than a quick sale.

More questions about Pennington County, SD Property Tax Guide

When are Pennington County property taxes due?

The first half is delinquent after April 30 and the second half after October 31. Taxes are paid one year in arrears and notices go out in late December or early January.

Does Pennington County hold a tax sale?

Only if the Board of Commissioners authorizes it. When held, it is on the third Monday of December, and none was held in 2023. Unpaid taxes produce a tax certificate first.

Where do I pay Pennington County property tax?

Pay at 900 Concourse Drive, Suite 150, in Rapid City, by mail to PO Box 6160, in a drop box, or online. Online fees are $1.95 for an e-check and 2% for cards.

What is the Pennington County senior freeze deadline?

Applications for the assessment freeze and the homestead deferral are due to the Treasurer's Office by April 1 each year.

Can I sell my Pennington County house with taxes owed?

Yes. The Treasurer gives a payoff figure, and the tax is paid from the proceeds at closing. Delinquent taxes require certified funds and no payment plans are accepted.

  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Lincoln County, SD Property Tax Guide sale
  • Turn the Lincoln County, SD Property Tax Guide offer down and you owe us nothing

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Lincoln County, South Dakota property tax involves the county assessment office and the county treasurer.

Who to contact in Lincoln County

  • Lincoln County Treasurer
  • Lincoln County Director of Equalization handles assessment and appeals.

Tax rate

South Dakota bills combine county, municipal and school district levies.

Selling in Lincoln County?
We buy Lincoln County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

What we could not confirm

  • Register of deeds not researched

Lincoln County by the numbers

The Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey counts 68,286 people and 27,552 housing units in Lincoln County, which ranks 3 of 3 South Dakota counties here. Median home value is $323,500, which is 44% above the middle county in this South Dakota set. Households here earn a median $96,552; the middle South Dakota county is at $70,101. 28% of occupied homes are rented, which leaves 72% owner-occupied. The median home was built in 2004, about 19 years ago.

Where is Lincoln County, South Dakota, and who lives there?

Lincoln County sits on South Dakota's eastern edge, with the Big Sioux River running along its eastern boundary and separating it from Iowa. The county covers 578 square miles of low rolling hills that slope toward the river valley, and it is still largely agricultural outside the towns.

The county was formed on December 30, 1867 and named for Abraham Lincoln. Canton is the county seat. Its population was 712 in 1870 and peaked at 13,918 in 1930. It dipped through the middle of the twentieth century, then grew sharply after 1980 and reached 65,161 in the 2020 census, which makes it the third most populous county in the state. Much of that growth is tied to Sioux Falls spreading south.

Towns and cities in or touching the county include Beresford (partly), Canton, Harrisburg, Lennox, Sioux Falls (partly), Tea, Worthing, Naomi (partly) and Norway Center. A house in a Sioux Falls neighborhood on the Lincoln County side is taxed through the same county offices as a farmhouse near Canton, but the city and school levies differ, which is why two Lincoln County sellers can see very different bills.

FactLincoln County
County seatCanton
FormedDecember 30, 1867
Total area578 square miles
Population, 2020 census65,161
Population, Census Bureau 2019-2023 survey68,286
Housing units, 2019-202327,552
Median home value, 2019-2023$323,500
Owner-occupied homes72%

Which offices handle property tax in Lincoln County?

Three offices matter: the Department of Equalization sets values, the Treasurer collects the money, and the Register of Deeds records the sale. The Lincoln County courthouse is at 104 N. Main Street in Canton and is open 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday, excluding holidays.

  • Department of Equalization: 104 North Main Street, Suite 210, Canton, SD 57013. Phone 605-764-2571. It handles assessments and is the first call if you think your value is wrong.
  • Treasurer: 104 N. Main Street, Canton, SD 57013. Phone 605-764-5701. It collects property tax and vehicle fees, and it helps people 65 or older and disabled residents apply for the tax freeze and rebate programs.
  • Register of Deeds: records the deed when a house changes hands. We did not find a Lincoln County fee page, so ask the office for its current schedule.

The treasurer's phone line runs 9:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., a little narrower than the counter hours. Title transfers and new title registrations must reach the Treasurer before 4:30 p.m. to be finished that day. You can read the county's own explanation on the Lincoln County property tax page.

When are Lincoln County property taxes due, and what does a late payment cost?

Lincoln County property tax is paid in two halves: the first half by April 30 and the second half by October 31, with payments postmarked by those dates counting as on time. Notices for real estate taxes and special assessments are mailed to owners in January.

State law sets the penalty. Under SDCL 10-21-23, one half of the unpaid real property tax becomes delinquent on May 1, and the other half on November 1 if it is still unpaid after October 31. Interest is added on the delinquency date and on the first day of each month after that, at the rate set under SDCL 54-3-16. Taxes totaling fifty dollars or less must be paid in full by April 30. If the last day of April or October falls on a weekend, the due date moves to the last working day of that month.

  • Mailed payments can take 5 to 7 business days to process.
  • Online payments can take 3 to 5 business days.
  • Online fees: $1.50 for an e-check, or 2.4% with a $1.50 minimum for a card or PayPal.
  • Delinquent taxes cannot be paid online. Contact the Treasurer's Office directly.

If you plan to sell, pay close attention to those posting times. A payment that clears after the deadline can carry interest into your closing figures.

How are Lincoln County homes valued and taxed?

South Dakota assesses property at market value, then taxes 85% of it. The Department of Revenue gives an example: a $230,000 home has a taxable value of $195,500. Each taxing unit, meaning the county, the city and the school district, sets a levy by dividing its unfunded budget by the taxable value in its area, and the tax on a property is its taxable value times the combined levy per thousand dollars.

The Lincoln County Department of Equalization values land and buildings. The state's own description says a building's value depends mainly on its quality, size, design and condition, and that extras count. Owner-occupied homes carry a separate tax classification. The home must be your primary residence on November 1, you can claim it on only one dwelling in the state, and you file the Certification of Owner-Occupied Dwelling with the county Director of Equalization by March 15.

For a sense of scale, the City of Harrisburg published its levies per $1,000 of taxable value for the 2019 tax year, payable in 2020: school 11.926, city 3.293 and county 2.128, for a total of 17.347. Those figures are old, and current levies differ, but they show how most of the bill goes to the school district. Check the current levy sheet before you estimate anything.

How do you appeal a Lincoln County assessment?

You appeal in steps, and each step has a hard date. Start by talking to the Lincoln County Department of Equalization at 605-764-2571, since many questions are settled by correcting the property record. If that does not work, file a written appeal. The deadlines below come from the Department of Revenue's 2025 guide, so confirm the current year's calendar with the county.

StepDate in the 2025 guide
Assessment notices mailedBy March 1
Owner-occupied filingMarch 15
Written appeal to the local board clerkMarch 13 (postmarked counts)
Local board meetsMarch 17 to March 21
Written appeal to the county auditor, for the county boardApril 1
County board of equalization sitsApril 8 to April 29
Letter to the Office of Hearing ExaminersMay 16

An appeal from the county board to circuit court must be made within 30 days after notice is served, and you cannot appeal to the hearing examiners and the circuit court at the same time. Sioux Falls residents in Lincoln County can schedule a local board appeal through the county's appeal page or the Sioux Falls City Clerk at 605-367-8080, and the hearings are held at Carnegie Town Hall, 235 W. 10th St. Remember what an appeal argues: that the value is too high or unequal. It does not reduce the tax rate.

What help exists for older or disabled Lincoln County owners?

South Dakota offers an assessment freeze for elderly and disabled homeowners, and the application is due to the county Treasurer by April 1 each year. Applicants must be 65 or older, or disabled, as of January 1, and must meet income guidelines that count all household income. The Treasurer's office helps with the forms, which are also on the Department of Revenue site.

This matters for sellers because a frozen value can make a long-held house look inexpensive to carry, and a buyer may not face the same bill. If you are selling a parent's house, ask the Treasurer whether a freeze was in place.

What should a Lincoln County seller check before closing?

Confirm what is owed to the Treasurer, then record the deed with the Register of Deeds. South Dakota charges a real estate transfer fee of $0.50 per $500 of value, which equals $1.00 per $1,000, under SDCL 43-4-21, and it applies to a deed only when there is consideration. The recording fee under SDCL 7-9-15 is $30 per document for the first 50 pages, and Lincoln County can confirm its current amounts.

  • The tax bill comes in January and is paid in two halves, so check which half is paid before you set a closing date.
  • Special assessments from a city, such as a storm water or maintenance fee collected on the tax roll, can sit on the bill separately.
  • South Dakota law treats unpaid taxes as a perpetual lien, so a title company will want them cleared or credited at closing.
  • Ask the Treasurer for a payoff figure for any delinquent amount. These cannot be paid online.

A cash buyer can close around these items without a long listing period, which helps if a bill is close to going delinquent. We buy houses as-is across the Sioux Falls area and Lincoln County and will give you a written offer to compare.

More questions about Lincoln County, SD Property Tax Guide

When are property taxes due in Lincoln County, SD?

The first half is due by April 30 and the second half by October 31. Payments must be postmarked by those dates to avoid interest, and notices are mailed in January.

Where do I pay Lincoln County property tax?

Pay the Treasurer at 104 N. Main Street in Canton, by mail, or online. Online fees are $1.50 for an e-check or 2.4% for a card. Delinquent taxes must be handled with the office directly.

Can I appeal my Lincoln County assessment?

Yes. Start with the Lincoln County Department of Equalization at 605-764-2571, then file a written appeal with the local or county board of equalization by the state deadlines, which fall in March and April.

Is there a tax freeze for seniors in Lincoln County?

Yes, the assessment freeze for the elderly and disabled. You must be 65 or older, or disabled, as of January 1, meet income limits, and apply to the Treasurer by April 1.

Can I sell my Lincoln County house if I owe property tax?

Yes. Unpaid taxes are paid or credited at closing from the sale proceeds. Ask the Treasurer for a payoff figure, and a cash sale can close quickly around it.
